The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

## Key Features ### Syntax highlighting `bat` supports syntax highlighting for a large number of programming and markup languages. ### Git integration `bat` communicates with `git` to show modifications with respect to the index. ### Show non-printable characters You can use the `-A`/`--show-all` option to show and highlight non-printable characters. ### Automatic paging By default, `bat` pipes its own output to a pager (e.g. `less`) if the output is too large for one screen. If you would rather `bat` work like `cat` all the time (never page output), you can set `--paging=never` as an option, either on the command line or in your configuration file. If you intend to alias `cat` to `bat` in your shell configuration, you can use `alias cat='bat --paging=never'` to preserve the default behavior. #### File concatenation Even with a pager set, you can still use `bat` to concatenate files. g # output 'f', then stdin, then 'g'. ``` ### Integration with other tools #### `fzf` You can use `bat` as a previewer for `fzf`: ```bash fzf --preview "bat --color=always --style=numbers --line-range=:500 {}" ``` #### `find` or `fd` Preview all search results with `bat`: ```bash find … -exec bat {} + fd … -X bat ``` #### `ripgrep` With `batgrep`, `bat` can be used as the printer for `ripgrep` search results: ```bash batgrep needle src/ ``` #### `tail -f` `bat` can be combined with `tail -f` to continuously monitor a given file with syntax highlighting: ```bash tail -f /var/log/pacman.log | bat --paging=never -l log ``` #### `git` Combine `bat` with `git show` to view an older version of a file with syntax highlighting: ```bash git show v0.6.0:src/main.rs | bat -l rs ``` #### `git diff` Combine `bat` with `git diff` to view lines around code changes: ```bash batdiff() { git diff --name-only --relative --diff-filter=d -z | xargs -0 bat --diff } ``` #### `xclip` Pipe the output into `xclip` to copy file contents: ```bash bat main.cpp | xclip ``` `bat` will detect that the output is being redirected and print the plain file contents. #### `man` `bat` can be used as a colorizing pager for `man`: ```bash export MANPAGER="bat -plman" man 2 select ``` #### Highlighting `--help` messages You can use `bat` to colorize help text: ```bash cp --help | bat -plhelp ``` Or use a wrapper: ```bash alias bathelp='bat --plain --language=help' help() { "$@" --help 2>&1 | bathelp } ``` ## Installation Download prebuilt binaries from the release page for your platform. `bat` is also available through various package managers: -     xterm-color|*-256color) color_prompt=yes;;
esac

# uncomment for a colored prompt, if the terminal has the capability; turned
# off by default to not distract the user: the focus in a terminal window
# should be on the output of commands, not on the prompt
#force_color_prompt=yes

if [ -n "$force_color_prompt" ]; then
    if [ -x /usr/bin/tput ] && tput setaf 1 >&/dev/null; then
	# We have color support; assume it's compliant with Ecma-48
	# (ISO/IEC-6429). (Lack of such support is extremely rare, and such
	# a case would tend to support setf rather than setaf.)
	color_prompt=yes
    else
	color_prompt=
    fi
fi

if [ "$color_prompt" = yes ]; then
    PS1='${debian_chroot:+($debian_chroot)}\[\033[01;32m\]\u@\h\[\033[00m\]:\[\033[01;34m\]\w\[\033[00m\]\$ '
else
    PS1='${debian_chroot:+($debian_chroot)}\u@\h:\w\$ '
fi
unset color_prompt force_color_prompt

# If this is an xterm set the title to user@host:dir
case "$TERM" in
xterm*|rxvt*)
    PS1="\[\e]0;${debian_chroot:+($debian_chroot)}\u@\h: \w\a\]$PS1"
    ;;
*)
    ;;
esac

# enable color support of ls and also add handy aliases
if [ -x /usr/bin/dircolors ]; then
    test -r ~/.dircolors && eval "$(dircolors -b ~/.dircolors)" || eval "$(dircolors -b)"
    alias ls='ls --color=auto'
    #alias dir='dir --color=auto'
    #alias vdir='vdir --color=auto'

    alias grep='grep --color=auto'
    alias fgrep='fgrep --color=auto'
    alias egrep='egrep --color=auto'
fi

# colored GCC warnings and errors
#export GCC_COLORS='error=01;31:warning=01;35:note=01;36:caret=01;32:locus=01:quote=01'

# some more ls aliases
alias ll='ls -alF'
alias la='ls -A'
alias l='ls -CF'

# Add an "alert" alias for long running commands.  Use like so:
#   sleep 10; alert
alias alert='notify-send --urgency=low -i "$([ $? = 0 ] && echo terminal || echo error)" "$(history|tail -n1|sed -e '\''s/^\s*[0-9]\+\s*//;s/[;&|]\s*alert$//'\'')"'

# You may want to put all your additions into a separate file like
# ~/.bash_aliases, instead of adding them here directly.
# See /usr/share/doc/bash-doc/examples in the bash-doc package.

if [ -f ~/.bash_aliases ]; then
    . ~/.bash_aliases
fi

# enable programmable completion features (you don't need to enable
# this, if it's already enabled in /etc/bash.bashrc and /etc/profile
# sources /etc/bash.bashrc).
if ! shopt -oq posix; then
  if [ -f /usr/share/bash-completion/bash_completion ]; then
    . /usr/share/bash-completion/bash_completion
  elif [ -f /etc/bash_completion ]; then
    . /etc/bash_completion
  fi
fi

# Parsing helpers for line ranges
def parse_line_range_spec(spec):
    spec = spec.strip()
    if not spec:
        raise ValueError("empty line range")
    # Split by colon, keep empty
    parts = spec.split(":")
    if len(parts) == 1:
        # single number
        s = parts[0]
        try:
            n = int(s)
            return (n, n, 0)
        except:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
    elif len(parts) == 2:
        start_s, end_s = parts
        # start
        start = None
        if start_s != "":
            try:
                start = int(start_s)
            except:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
        # end
        end = None
        ctx = 0
        if end_s != "":
            if end_s.startswith("+"):
                if start is None:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                try:
                    offset = int(end_s[1:])
                    end = start + offset
                except:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
            else:
                try:
                    end = int(end_s)
                except:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
        return (start, end, ctx)
    elif len(parts) == 3:
        start_s, end_s, ctx_s = parts
        start = None
        end = None
        ctx = 0
        if start_s != "":
            try:
                start = int(start_s)
            except:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
        if end_s != "":
            if end_s.startswith("+"):
                if start is None:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                try:
                    offset = int(end_s[1:])
                    end = start + offset
                except:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
            else:
                try:
                    end = int(end_s)
                except:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
        if ctx_s != "":
            try:
                ctx = int(ctx_s)
            except:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range context: {spec}")
        return (start, end, ctx)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")

def expand_ranges(ranges, total):
    # ranges: list of (start, end, ctx)
    # total: number of lines
    expanded = []
    for start, end, ctx in ranges:
        s = start
        e = end
        # Handle negative
        if s is not None and s < 0:
            s = total + s + 1
        if e is not None and e < 0:
            e = total + e + 1
        if s is None:
            s = 1
        if e is None:
            e = total
        # Clamp
        if s < 1:
            s = 1
        if e < 1:
            e = 1
        if s > total:
            s = total + 1  # will produce empty
        if e > total:
            e = total
        # Apply context
        if ctx:
            s = max(1, s - ctx)
            e = min(total, e + ctx)
        if s <= e:
            expanded.append((s,e))
    # Merge overlapping? Original bat merges? It also draws snip between non-consecutive ranges.
    # We'll keep sorted and merged for checking inclusion, but need to keep original for snip detection.
    # For inclusion check, we need merged.
    if not expanded:
        return []
    expanded_sorted = sorted(expanded)
    merged = [expanded_sorted[0]]
    for cur in expanded_sorted[1:]:
        prev = merged[-1]
        if cur[0] <= prev[1] + 1:
            merged[-1] = (prev[0], max(prev[1], cur[1]))
        else:
            merged.append(cur)
    return merged, expanded_sorted  # merged for inclusion, sorted for snip? Actually need to know gaps

def parse_highlight_spec(spec):
    spec = spec.strip()
    if not spec:
        raise ValueError("empty highlight")
    parts = spec.split(":")
    if len(parts) == 1:
        try:
            n = int(parts[0])
            return (n, n)
        except:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid highlight: {spec}")
    elif len(parts) == 2:
        start_s, end_s = parts
        start = None
        end = None
        if start_s == "":
            start = 1
        else:
            try:
                start = int(start_s)
            except:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid highlight: {spec}")
        if end_s == "":
            end = float('inf')
        else:
            if end_s.startswith("+"):
                try:
                    offset = int(end_s[1:])
                    end = start + offset
                except:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid highlight: {spec}")
            else:
                try:
                    end = int(end_s)
                except:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid highlight: {spec}")
        return (start, end)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid highlight: {spec}")

def is_highlighted_line(ln, hl_ranges):
    for s,e in hl_ranges:
        if e == float('inf'):
            if ln >= s:
                return True
        else:
            if s <= ln <= e:
                return True
    return False

def parse_terminal_width(val, default=80):
    # val can be like "80", "+10", "-10"
    # If prefixed with + or -, offset to actual terminal width
    # Actual terminal width: try to get from env or default 80?
    # For simplicity, use default 80 as base if not detected
    # Try to get terminal width via shutil.get_terminal_size
    import shutil
    try:
        cols = shutil.get_terminal_size().columns
    except:
        cols = default
    if val is None:
        return cols
    val = str(val).strip()
    if val.startswith("+") or val.startswith("-"):
        try:
            offset = int(val)
            return max(1, cols + offset)
        except:
            return cols
    else:
        try:
            return int(val)
        except:
            return cols

    # Not modify mode: replace

    result = set()

        # Strip +/-? If not all_modify but some have +/-?

            is_add = raw.startswith("+")

            val = STYLE_ALIASES[comp]
            if val == "":
                if is_add:
                    # plain: clear
                    if comp == "plain":
                        result.clear()
                else:
                    # -plain? what? ignore
                    pass
            else:
                # Expand alias
                for sub in val.split(","):
                    sub = sub.strip()
                    if not sub:
                        continue
                    # Resolve sub alias again
                    if sub in STYLE_ALIASES and sub in ["header"]:
                        sub = STYLE_ALIASES[sub]
                    if sub in VALID_STYLES:
                        if is_add:
                            result.add(sub)
                        else:
                            result.discard(sub)
                    else:
                        # sub may be like header-filename etc
                        if sub in VALID_STYLES:
                            if is_add:
                                result.add(sub)
                            else:
                                result.discard(sub)
                        else:
                            # Could be default expanded already includes valid? But for "default" alias expansion it's comma list includes header-filename etc, which we handle
                            # For "auto" etc
                            if sub == "":

                            # Might be recursive? For simplicity, if sub is still alias (like header), resolve

        else:

            if comp == "header":

            if comp not in VALID_STYLES and comp not in ["default","full","auto","plain"]:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown style '{comp}'")
            if comp in VALID_STYLES:
                if is_add:
                    result.add(comp)
                else:
                    result.discard(comp)
    # Order result
    # Keep order as per FULL_STYLE order for consistency
    ordered = [c for c in FULL_STYLE if c in result]
    # Also include any not in FULL_STYLE (should not)
    for c in result:
        if c not in ordered:

def tab_placeholder(width):

    # From earlier observed:
    # width 0,1,2,... mapping
    # width 1 -> ↹ (single char)
    # width 2 -> ├┤
    # width 3 -> ├─┤
    # width 4 -> ├──┤
    # width 8 -> ├──────┤ (dash count = width-2? Let's see: width 4 has 2 dashes? Actually "├──┤" contains 2 box drawing horiz lines? The string "├──┤" is: '├', '─', '─', '┤' => 2 dashes for width 4? For width 8 we saw 6 dashes. So dashes = width-2.

    # if width == 0: treat as 4? Or maybe tab width 0 is ignored and shows as 4? But our earlier test showed width 0 -> "├──┤" which is width 4 placeholder. So we will treat 0 as 4 for show-all.
    if width == 0:

# Parsing helpers for line ranges
def parse_line_range_spec(spec):
    spec = spec.strip()
    if not spec:
        raise ValueError("empty line range")
    # Split by colon, keep empty
    parts = spec.split(":")
    if len(parts) == 1:
        # single number
        s = parts[0]
        try:
            n = int(s)
            return (n, n, 0)
        except:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
    elif len(parts) == 2:
        start_s, end_s = parts
        # start
        start = None
        if start_s != "":
            try:
                start = int(start_s)
            except:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
        # end
        end = None
        ctx = 0
        if end_s != "":
            if end_s.startswith("+"):
                if start is None:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                try:
                    offset = int(end_s[1:])
                    end = start + offset
                except:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
            else:
                try:
                    end = int(end_s)
                except:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
        return (start, end, ctx)
    elif len(parts) == 3:
        start_s, end_s, ctx_s = parts
        start = None
        end = None
        ctx = 0
        if start_s != "":
            try:
                start = int(start_s)
            except:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
        if end_s != "":
            if end_s.startswith("+"):
                if start is None:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                try:
                    offset = int(end_s[1:])
                    end = start + offset
                except:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
            else:
                try:
                    end = int(end_s)
                except:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
        if ctx_s != "":
            try:
                ctx = int(ctx_s)
            except:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range context: {spec}")
        return (start, end, ctx)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")

def expand_ranges(ranges, total):
    # ranges: list of (start, end, ctx)
    # total: number of lines
    expanded = []
    for start, end, ctx in ranges:
        s = start
        e = end
        # Handle negative
        if s is not None and s < 0:
            s = total + s + 1
        if e is not None and e < 0:
            e = total + e + 1
        if s is None:
            s = 1
        if e is None:
            e = total
        # Clamp
        if s < 1:
            s = 1
        if e < 1:
            e = 1
        if s > total:
            s = total + 1  # will produce empty
        if e > total:
            e = total
        # Apply context
        if ctx:
            s = max(1, s - ctx)
            e = min(total, e + ctx)
        if s <= e:
            expanded.append((s,e))
    # Merge overlapping? Original bat merges? It also draws snip between non-consecutive ranges.
    # We'll keep sorted and merged for checking inclusion, but need to keep original for snip detection.
    # For inclusion check, we need merged.
    if not expanded:
        return []
    expanded_sorted = sorted(expanded)
    merged = [expanded_sorted[0]]
    for cur in expanded_sorted[1:]:
        prev = merged[-1]
        if cur[0] <= prev[1] + 1:
            merged[-1] = (prev[0], max(prev[1], cur[1]))
        else:
            merged.append(cur)
    return merged, expanded_sorted  # merged for inclusion, sorted for snip? Actually need to know gaps

def parse_highlight_spec(spec):
    spec = spec.strip()
    if not spec:
        raise ValueError("empty highlight")
    parts = spec.split(":")
    if len(parts) == 1:
        try:
            n = int(parts[0])
            return (n, n)
        except:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid highlight: {spec}")
    elif len(parts) == 2:
        start_s, end_s = parts
        start = None
        end = None
        if start_s == "":
            start = 1
        else:
            try:
                start = int(start_s)
            except:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid highlight: {spec}")
        if end_s == "":
            end = float('inf')
        else:
            if end_s.startswith("+"):
                try:
                    offset = int(end_s[1:])
                    end = start + offset
                except:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid highlight: {spec}")
            else:
                try:
                    end = int(end_s)
                except:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid highlight: {spec}")
        return (start, end)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid highlight: {spec}")

def is_highlighted_line(ln, hl_ranges):
    for s,e in hl_ranges:
        if e == float('inf'):
            if ln >= s:
                return True
        else:
            if s <= ln <= e:
                return True
    return False

def parse_terminal_width(val, default=80):
    # val can be like "80", "+10", "-10"
    # If prefixed with + or -, offset to actual terminal width
    # Actual terminal width: try to get from env or default 80?
    # For simplicity, use default 80 as base if not detected
    # Try to get terminal width via shutil.get_terminal_size
    import shutil
    try:
        cols = shutil.get_terminal_size().columns
    except:
        cols = default
    if val is None:
        return cols
    val = str(val).strip()
    if val.startswith("+") or val.startswith("-"):
        try:
            offset = int(val)
            return max(1, cols + offset)
        except:
            return cols
    else:
        try:
            return int(val)
        except:
            return cols

def expand_tabs(line, tab_width):
    if tab_width == 0:
        return line
    # Expand \t to spaces up to next tab stop
    # Tab stop every tab_width columns
    result = []
    col = 0
    for ch in line:
        if ch == '\t':
            spaces = tab_width - (col % tab_width)
            result.append(' ' * spaces)
            col += spaces
        else:
            result.append(ch)
            col += 1
    return "".join(result)

    # We'll implement simple state machine
    args = ParsedArgs()
    i=0
    # For handling '--' separator
    end_of_options = False
    while i < len(argv):
        tok = argv[i]
        if end_of_options:

            i+=1
            continue
        if tok == "--":

            i+=1
            continue

# Tab placeholder
def tab_placeholder(width):
    if width==0:
        width=4
    if width==1:
        return "↹"
    if width==2:
        return "├┤"
    if width>=3:
        return "├" + "─"*(width-2) + "┤"
    return "↹"

def expand_tabs_simple(line, tab_width):
    if tab_width==0:
        return line
    result=[]
    col=0
    for ch in line:
        if ch=='\t':
            spaces = tab_width - (col % tab_width)
            result.append(' '*spaces)
            col+=spaces
        else:
            result.append(ch)
            col+=1
    return "".join(result)

def show_all_line(line_str, notation, tab_width):
    # line_str is str without trailing \n
    # transform
    res=[]
    for ch in line_str:
        if ch==' ':
            res.append('·')
        elif ch=='\t':
            res.append(tab_placeholder(tab_width))
        else:
            o=ord(ch)
            if o==0:
                res.append('␀' if notation=='unicode' else '^@')
            elif 1<=o<=31:
                if o==10:
                    res.append('␊' if notation=='unicode' else '^J')
                elif o==13:
                    res.append('␍' if notation=='unicode' else '^M')
                else:
                    if notation=='unicode':
                        res.append(chr(0x2400+o))
                    else:
                        if o==0:
                            res.append('^@')
                        else:
                            # caret
                            # For visual, use ^A etc
                            if 1<=o<=26:
                                res.append('^'+chr(64+o))
                            elif o==27:
                                res.append('^[')
                            elif o==28:
                                res.append('^\\')
                            elif o==29:
                                res.append('^]')
                            elif o==30:
                                res.append('^^')
                            elif o==31:
                                res.append('^_')
                            else:
                                res.append(chr(0x2400+o))
            elif o==127:
                res.append('␡' if notation=='unicode' else '^?')
            elif o>=128:
                # For simplicity, if printable, keep, else escape \x
                if ch.isprintable():
                    res.append(ch)
                else:
                    res.append(f"\\x{o:02X}")
            else:
                res.append(ch)
    return "".join(res)

def show_all_bytes(data_bytes, notation, tab_width):
    # data_bytes: bytes for one line (without newline char? But may include \r)
    # We'll try to decode as utf-8, if fails escape high bytes
    try:
        text = data_bytes.decode('utf-8')
        return show_all_line(text, notation, tab_width)
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        res=[]
        for b in data_bytes:
            if b==32:
                res.append('·')
            elif b==9:
                res.append(tab_placeholder(tab_width))
            elif b==10:
                res.append('␊' if notation=='unicode' else '^J')
            elif b==13:
                res.append('␍' if notation=='unicode' else '^M')
            elif b<32:
                if notation=='unicode':
                    res.append(chr(0x2400+b))
                else:
                    if b==0:
                        res.append('^@')
                    else:
                        res.append('^'+chr(64+b) if 1<=b<=26 else chr(0x2400+b))
            elif b==127:
                res.append('␡' if notation=='unicode' else '^?')
            elif b<128:
                res.append(chr(b))
            else:
                res.append(f"\\x{b:02X}")
        return "".join(res)

def parse_line_range_for_file(ranges, total):
    # ranges: list of spec strings
    # returns (merged_ranges, original_sorted_ranges) where merged is list of (s,e) inclusive
    # and also original sorted for snip detection? We'll just return merged and also expanded list of individual ranges before merge sorted
    parsed=[]
    for spec in ranges:
        spec=spec.strip()
        if not spec:
            continue
        parts=spec.split(":")
        if len(parts)==1:
            try:
                n=int(parts[0])
                parsed.append((n,n,0))
            except:
                eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                sys.exit(1)
        elif len(parts)==2:
            start_s,end_s=parts
            start=None
            end=None
            if start_s!="":
                try:
                    start=int(start_s)
                except:
                    eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                    sys.exit(1)
            if end_s!="":
                if end_s.startswith("+"):
                    if start is None:
                        eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                        sys.exit(1)
                    try:
                        offset=int(end_s[1:])
                        end=start+offset
                    except:
                        eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                        sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    try:
                        end=int(end_s)
                    except:
                        eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                        sys.exit(1)
            parsed.append((start,end,0))
        elif len(parts)==3:
            start_s,end_s,ctx_s=parts
            start=None
            end=None
            ctx=0
            if start_s!="":
                try:
                    start=int(start_s)
                except:
                    eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                    sys.exit(1)
            if end_s!="":
                if end_s.startswith("+"):
                    if start is None:
                        eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                        sys.exit(1)
                    try:
                        offset=int(end_s[1:])
                        end=start+offset
                    except:
                        eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                        sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    try:
                        end=int(end_s)
                    except:
                        eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                        sys.exit(1)
            if ctx_s!="":
                try:
                    ctx=int(ctx_s)
                except:
                    eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                    sys.exit(1)
            parsed.append((start,end,ctx))
        else:
            eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
            sys.exit(1)
    # Expand with total
    expanded=[]
    for start,end,ctx in parsed:
        s=start
        e=end
        if s is not None and s<0:
            s=total+s+1
        if e is not None and e<0:
            e=total+e+1
        if s is None:
            s=1
        if e is None:
            e=total
        if s<1:
            s=1
        if e<1:
            e=1
        if s>total:
            continue
        if e>total:
            e=total
        s=max(1,s-ctx)
        e=min(total,e+ctx)
        if s<=e:
            expanded.append((s,e))
    if not expanded:
        return [], []
    expanded_sorted=sorted(expanded)
    merged=[expanded_sorted[0]]
    for cur in expanded_sorted[1:]:
        prev=merged[-1]
        if cur[0]<=prev[1]+1:
            merged[-1]=(prev[0],max(prev[1],cur[1]))
        else:
            merged.append(cur)
    return merged, expanded_sorted

def parse_highlight_ranges(specs, total_lines=None):
    # returns list of (s,e) with e=inf allowed
    res=[]
    for spec in specs:
        spec=spec.strip()
        if not spec:
            continue
        parts=spec.split(":")
        if len(parts)==1:
            try:
                n=int(parts[0])
                res.append((n,n))
            except:
                eprint_error(f"Invalid highlight line: {spec}")
                sys.exit(1)
        elif len(parts)==2:
            start_s,end_s=parts
            start=None
            end=None
            if start_s=="":
                start=1
            else:
                try:
                    start=int(start_s)
                except:
                    eprint_error(f"Invalid highlight line: {spec}")
                    sys.exit(1)
            if end_s=="":
                end=float('inf')
            else:
                if end_s.startswith("+"):
                    try:
                        offset=int(end_s[1:])
                        end=start+offset
                    except:
                        eprint_error(f"Invalid highlight line: {spec}")
                        sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    try:
                        end=int(end_s)
                    except:
                        eprint_error(f"Invalid highlight line: {spec}")
                        sys.exit(1)
            if isinstance(end,float):
                res.append((start,end))
            else:
                if start>end:
                    start,end=end,start
                res.append((start,end))
        else:
            eprint_error(f"Invalid highlight line: {spec}")
            sys.exit(1)
    return res

def is_highlighted(ln, hl_ranges):
    for s,e in hl_ranges:
        if e==float('inf'):
            if ln>=s:
                return True
        else:
            if s<=ln<=e:
                return True
    return False

def read_config_file(path):
    opts=[]
    try:
        with open(path,'r',encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore') as f:
            for line in f:
                stripped=line.strip()
                if not stripped or stripped.startswith('#'):
                    continue
                try:
                    parts=shlex.split(stripped, comments=False)
                    opts.extend(parts)
                except:
                    opts.extend(stripped.split())
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass
    return opts

def get_bat_opts():
    v=os.environ.get("BAT_OPTS")
    if not v:
        return []
    try:
        return shlex.split(v)
    except:
        return v.split()

FULL_STYLE = ["changes","grid","header-filename","header-filesize","numbers","snip","rule"]

def resolve_style_alias(name):
    if name=="header":
        return ["header-filename"]
    if name=="default":
        return DEFAULT_STYLE[:]
    if name=="full":
        return FULL_STYLE[:]
    if name=="auto":
        return DEFAULT_STYLE[:]  # will be handled as auto later, but for now default
    if name=="plain":
        return []
    return [name]

def parse_style_list(raw_values, env_style=None, is_tty=False, decorations="auto"):
    # raw_values: list of style strings from config, env, command line in order of precedence (earliest lowest)
    # We need to apply precedence: command line highest, then env, then config
    # For this function, we receive all raw values in order low to high, and we need to compute final style
    # Also handle + - modifiers
    # If any raw value consists entirely of +/- prefixed components, it modifies previous
    # else it replaces
    current = None  # None means not set yet, will use default
    # We'll iterate
    for raw in raw_values:
        raw = raw.strip()
        if not raw:
            current = []
            continue
        parts = [p.strip() for p in raw.split(",") if p.strip()!=""]
        if not parts:
            current = []
            continue
        # Check if all parts start with + or -
        all_mod = all(p.startswith("+") or p.startswith("-") for p in parts)
        if all_mod and current is not None:
            # modify
            cur_set = set(current)
            for p in parts:
                sign = p[0]
                comp = p[1:]
                # resolve alias
                alias_expanded = resolve_style_alias(comp) if comp in ("header","default","full","auto","plain") else [comp]
                # For plain alias, expanded [] -> special handling
                if comp=="plain":
                    if sign=="+":
                        # +plain? means add plain? That would clear? Actually +plain doesn't make sense; but handle as clear?
                        cur_set.clear()
                    else:
                        # -plain? maybe nothing
                        pass
                    continue
                if comp=="default":
                    # default expands to list, but with +/- meaning add/remove those?
                    expanded = DEFAULT_STYLE
                elif comp=="full":
                    expanded = FULL_STYLE
                elif comp=="auto":
                    expanded = DEFAULT_STYLE
                elif comp=="header":
                    expanded = ["header-filename"]
                elif comp in ("changes","grid","header-filename","header-filesize","numbers","snip","rule"):
                    expanded = [comp]
                else:
                    # unknown
                    eprint_error(f"Unknown style '{comp}'")
                    sys.exit(1)
                if sign=="+":
                    for e in expanded:
                        cur_set.add(e)
                else:
                    for e in expanded:
                        cur_set.discard(e)
            current = list(cur_set)
        else:
            # replace
            new_set = set()
            for p in parts:
                # p may have +/- but if not all_mod, we treat as replace starting empty, but +/- still affects empty?
                # For simplicity, handle +/- even in replace: + adds, - removes (from empty, removing does nothing)
                if p.startswith("+") or p.startswith("-"):
                    sign = p[0]
                    comp = p[1:]
                    if comp in ("header","default","full","auto","plain"):
                        if comp=="plain":
                            if sign=="+":
                                new_set.clear()
                            continue
                        elif comp=="default":
                            expanded = DEFAULT_STYLE
                        elif comp=="full":
                            expanded = FULL_STYLE
                        elif comp=="auto":
                            expanded = DEFAULT_STYLE
                        elif comp=="header":
                            expanded = ["header-filename"]
                        else:
                            expanded=[]
                    else:
                        if comp in ("changes","grid","header-filename","header-filesize","numbers","snip","rule"):
                            expanded=[comp]
                        else:
                            eprint_error(f"Unknown style '{comp}'")
                            sys.exit(1)
                    if sign=="+":
                        for e in expanded:
                            new_set.add(e)
                    else:
                        for e in expanded:
                            new_set.discard(e)
                else:
                    # no sign
                    if p in ("header","default","full","auto","plain"):
                        if p=="plain":
                            new_set.clear()
                        elif p=="default":
                            new_set.update(DEFAULT_STYLE)
                        elif p=="full":
                            new_set.update(FULL_STYLE)
                        elif p=="auto":
                            new_set.update(DEFAULT_STYLE)
                        elif p=="header":
                            new_set.add("header-filename")
                    else:
                        if p not in ("changes","grid","header-filename","header-filesize","numbers","snip","rule"):
                            eprint_error(f"Unknown style '{p}'")
                            sys.exit(1)
                        new_set.add(p)
            current = list(new_set)

def parse_args(argv):
    # argv is list of args (excluding program name), but may include config file options prepended
    # We'll implement simple state machine
    args = ParsedArgs()
    i=0
    # For handling '--' separator
    end_of_options = False
    while i < len(argv):
        tok = argv[i]
        if end_of_options:
            args.files.append(tok)
            i+=1
            continue
        if tok == "--":
            end_of_options = True
            i+=1
            continue
        # Short options combined? e.g., -pp, -An etc
        if tok.startswith("-") and not tok.startswith("--") and len(tok)>1:
            # Handle combined short flags
            # Valid short: A p l H d S n m s r L u E h V P f
            # Some take args: l, H, m, r, etc
            # We need to iterate chars
            # If tok == "-P" alone -> paging never
            # If tok == "-f" -> force-color
            # Implementation: go through chars
            j=1
            while j < len(tok):
                ch = tok[j]
                if ch == 'A':
                    args.show_all = True
                elif ch == 'p':
                    args.plain_count += 1
                elif ch == 'l':
                    # language needs arg
                    # If remaining chars in tok after l, treat as arg? In clap, -lPython would be value. Let's support.
                    if j+1 < len(tok):
                        args.language = tok[j+1:]
                        break
                    else:
                        i+=1
                        if i < len(argv):
                            args.language = argv[i]
                        else:
                            eprint_error("A value is required for '-l, --language <language>' but none was supplied")
                            sys.exit(1)
                    # break after consuming
                elif ch == 'H':
                    if j+1 < len(tok):
                        args.highlight_lines.append(tok[j+1:])
                        break
                    else:
                        i+=1
                        if i < len(argv):
                            args.highlight_lines.append(argv[i])
                        else:
                            eprint_error("A value is required for '-H, --highlight-line <N:M>' but none was supplied")
                            sys.exit(1)
                elif ch == 'd':
                    args.diff = True
                elif ch == 'S':
                    args.chop_long_lines = True
                elif ch == 'n':
                    args.number = True
                elif ch == 'm':
                    if j+1 < len(tok):
                        args.map_syntax.append(tok[j+1:])
                        break
                    else:
                        i+=1
                        if i < len(argv):
                            args.map_syntax.append(argv[i])
                        else:
                            eprint_error("A value is required for '-m, --map-syntax <glob:syntax>' but none was supplied")
                            sys.exit(1)
                elif ch == 's':
                    args.squeeze_blank = True
                elif ch == 'r':
                    if j+1 < len(tok):
                        args.line_ranges.append(tok[j+1:])
                        break
                    else:
                        i+=1
                        if i < len(argv):
                            args.line_ranges.append(argv[i])
                        else:
                            eprint_error("A value is required for '-r, --line-range <N:M>' but none was supplied")
                            sys.exit(1)
                elif ch == 'L':
                    args.list_languages = True
                elif ch == 'u':
                    args.unbuffered = True
                elif ch == 'E':
                    args.quiet_empty = True
                elif ch == 'h':
                    args.help_short = True
                elif ch == 'V':
                    args.version = True
                elif ch == 'P':
                    args.no_paging = True
                    args.paging = "never"
                elif ch == 'f':
                    args.force_colorization = True
                else:
                    eprint_error(f"Unexpected argument '-{ch}' found")
                    sys.exit(2)
                j+=1
            i+=1
            continue
        # Long options
        if tok.startswith("--"):
            # Split --opt=value
            if "=" in tok:
                opt, val = tok.split("=",1)
            else:
                opt, val = tok, None
            # Map opt
            if opt in ("--show-all",):
                args.show_all = True

                        sys.exit(1)

                    sys.exit(1)

# Tab placeholder
def tab_placeholder(width):
    if width==0:
        width=4
    if width==1:
        return "↹"
    if width==2:
        return "├┤"
    if width>=3:
        return "├" + "─"*(width-2) + "┤"
    return "↹"

def expand_tabs_simple(line, tab_width):
    if tab_width==0:
        return line
    result=[]
    col=0
    for ch in line:
        if ch=='\t':
            spaces = tab_width - (col % tab_width)
            result.append(' '*spaces)
            col+=spaces
        else:
            result.append(ch)
            col+=1
    return "".join(result)

def show_all_line(line_str, notation, tab_width):
    # line_str is str without trailing \n
    # transform
    res=[]
    for ch in line_str:
        if ch==' ':
            res.append('·')
        elif ch=='\t':
            res.append(tab_placeholder(tab_width))
        else:
            o=ord(ch)
            if o==0:
                res.append('␀' if notation=='unicode' else '^@')
            elif 1<=o<=31:
                if o==10:
                    res.append('␊' if notation=='unicode' else '^J')
                elif o==13:
                    res.append('␍' if notation=='unicode' else '^M')
                else:
                    if notation=='unicode':
                        res.append(chr(0x2400+o))
                    else:
                        if o==0:
                            res.append('^@')
                        else:
                            # caret
                            # For visual, use ^A etc
                            if 1<=o<=26:
                                res.append('^'+chr(64+o))
                            elif o==27:
                                res.append('^[')
                            elif o==28:
                                res.append('^\\')
                            elif o==29:
                                res.append('^]')
                            elif o==30:
                                res.append('^^')
                            elif o==31:
                                res.append('^_')
                            else:
                                res.append(chr(0x2400+o))
            elif o==127:
                res.append('␡' if notation=='unicode' else '^?')
            elif o>=128:
                # For simplicity, if printable, keep, else escape \x
                if ch.isprintable():
                    res.append(ch)
                else:
                    res.append(f"\\x{o:02X}")
            else:
                res.append(ch)
    return "".join(res)

def show_all_bytes(data_bytes, notation, tab_width):
    # data_bytes: bytes for one line (without newline char? But may include \r)
    # We'll try to decode as utf-8, if fails escape high bytes
    try:
        text = data_bytes.decode('utf-8')
        return show_all_line(text, notation, tab_width)
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        res=[]
        for b in data_bytes:
            if b==32:
                res.append('·')
            elif b==9:
                res.append(tab_placeholder(tab_width))
            elif b==10:
                res.append('␊' if notation=='unicode' else '^J')
            elif b==13:
                res.append('␍' if notation=='unicode' else '^M')
            elif b<32:
                if notation=='unicode':
                    res.append(chr(0x2400+b))
                else:
                    if b==0:
                        res.append('^@')
                    else:
                        res.append('^'+chr(64+b) if 1<=b<=26 else chr(0x2400+b))
            elif b==127:
                res.append('␡' if notation=='unicode' else '^?')
            elif b<128:
                res.append(chr(b))
            else:
                res.append(f"\\x{b:02X}")
        return "".join(res)

def parse_line_range_for_file(ranges, total):
    # ranges: list of spec strings
    # returns (merged_ranges, original_sorted_ranges) where merged is list of (s,e) inclusive
    # and also original sorted for snip detection? We'll just return merged and also expanded list of individual ranges before merge sorted
    parsed=[]
    for spec in ranges:
        spec=spec.strip()
        if not spec:
            continue
        parts=spec.split(":")
        if len(parts)==1:
            try:
                n=int(parts[0])
                parsed.append((n,n,0))
            except:
                eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                sys.exit(1)
        elif len(parts)==2:
            start_s,end_s=parts
            start=None
            end=None
            if start_s!="":
                try:
                    start=int(start_s)
                except:
                    eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                    sys.exit(1)
            if end_s!="":
                if end_s.startswith("+"):
                    if start is None:
                        eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                        sys.exit(1)
                    try:
                        offset=int(end_s[1:])
                        end=start+offset
                    except:
                        eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                        sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    try:
                        end=int(end_s)
                    except:
                        eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                        sys.exit(1)
            parsed.append((start,end,0))
        elif len(parts)==3:
            start_s,end_s,ctx_s=parts
            start=None
            end=None
            ctx=0
            if start_s!="":
                try:
                    start=int(start_s)
                except:
                    eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                    sys.exit(1)
            if end_s!="":
                if end_s.startswith("+"):
                    if start is None:
                        eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                        sys.exit(1)
                    try:
                        offset=int(end_s[1:])
                        end=start+offset
                    except:
                        eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                        sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    try:
                        end=int(end_s)
                    except:
                        eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                        sys.exit(1)
            if ctx_s!="":
                try:
                    ctx=int(ctx_s)
                except:
                    eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
                    sys.exit(1)
            parsed.append((start,end,ctx))
        else:
            eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}")
            sys.exit(1)
    # Expand with total
    expanded=[]
    for start,end,ctx in parsed:
        s=start
        e=end
        if s is not None and s<0:
            s=total+s+1
        if e is not None and e<0:
            e=total+e+1
        if s is None:
            s=1
        if e is None:
            e=total
        if s<1:
            s=1
        if e<1:
            e=1
        if s>total:
            continue
        if e>total:
            e=total
        s=max(1,s-ctx)
        e=min(total,e+ctx)
        if s<=e:
            expanded.append((s,e))
    if not expanded:
        return [], []
    expanded_sorted=sorted(expanded)
    merged=[expanded_sorted[0]]
    for cur in expanded_sorted[1:]:
        prev=merged[-1]
        if cur[0]<=prev[1]+1:
            merged[-1]=(prev[0],max(prev[1],cur[1]))
        else:
            merged.append(cur)
    return merged, expanded_sorted

def parse_highlight_ranges(specs, total_lines=None):
    # returns list of (s,e) with e=inf allowed
    res=[]
    for spec in specs:
        spec=spec.strip()
        if not spec:
            continue
        parts=spec.split(":")
        if len(parts)==1:
            try:
                n=int(parts[0])
                res.append((n,n))
            except:
                eprint_error(f"Invalid highlight line: {spec}")
                sys.exit(1)
        elif len(parts)==2:
            start_s,end_s=parts
            start=None
            end=None
            if start_s=="":
                start=1
            else:
                try:
                    start=int(start_s)
                except:
                    eprint_error(f"Invalid highlight line: {spec}")
                    sys.exit(1)
            if end_s=="":
                end=float('inf')
            else:
                if end_s.startswith("+"):
                    try:
                        offset=int(end_s[1:])
                        end=start+offset
                    except:
                        eprint_error(f"Invalid highlight line: {spec}")
                        sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    try:
                        end=int(end_s)
                    except:
                        eprint_error(f"Invalid highlight line: {spec}")
                        sys.exit(1)
            if isinstance(end,float):
                res.append((start,end))
            else:
                if start>end:
                    start,end=end,start
                res.append((start,end))
        else:
            eprint_error(f"Invalid highlight line: {spec}")
            sys.exit(1)
    return res

def is_highlighted(ln, hl_ranges):
    for s,e in hl_ranges:
        if e==float('inf'):
            if ln>=s:
                return True
        else:
            if s<=ln<=e:
                return True
    return False

def read_config_file(path):
    opts=[]
    try:
        with open(path,'r',encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore') as f:
            for line in f:
                stripped=line.strip()
                if not stripped or stripped.startswith('#'):
                    continue
                try:
                    parts=shlex.split(stripped, comments=False)
                    opts.extend(parts)
                except:
                    opts.extend(stripped.split())
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass
    return opts

def get_bat_opts():
    v=os.environ.get("BAT_OPTS")
    if not v:
        return []
    try:
        return shlex.split(v)
    except:
        return v.split()

def resolve_style_alias(name):
    if name=="header":
        return ["header-filename"]
    if name=="default":
        return DEFAULT_STYLE[:]
    if name=="full":

def parse_style_list(raw_values, env_style=None, is_tty=False, decorations="auto"):
    # raw_values: list of style strings from config, env, command line in order of precedence (earliest lowest)
    # We need to apply precedence: command line highest, then env, then config
    # For this function, we receive all raw values in order low to high, and we need to compute final style
    # Also handle + - modifiers
    # If any raw value consists entirely of +/- prefixed components, it modifies previous
    # else it replaces
    current = None  # None means not set yet, will use default
    # We'll iterate
    for raw in raw_values:
        raw = raw.strip()
        if not raw:
            current = []
            continue
        parts = [p.strip() for p in raw.split(",") if p.strip()!=""]
        if not parts:
            current = []
            continue
        # Check if all parts start with + or -
        all_mod = all(p.startswith("+") or p.startswith("-") for p in parts)
        if all_mod and current is not None:
            # modify
            cur_set = set(current)
            for p in parts:
                sign = p[0]
                comp = p[1:]
                # resolve alias
                alias_expanded = resolve_style_alias(comp) if comp in ("header","default","full","auto","plain") else [comp]
                # For plain alias, expanded [] -> special handling
                if comp=="plain":
                    if sign=="+":
                        # +plain? means add plain? That would clear? Actually +plain doesn't make sense; but handle as clear?
                        cur_set.clear()
                    else:
                        # -plain? maybe nothing
                        pass
                    continue
                if comp=="default":
                    # default expands to list, but with +/- meaning add/remove those?
                    expanded = DEFAULT_STYLE
                elif comp=="full":
                    expanded = FULL_STYLE
                elif comp=="auto":
                    expanded = DEFAULT_STYLE
                elif comp=="header":
                    expanded = ["header-filename"]
                elif comp in ("changes","grid","header-filename","header-filesize","numbers","snip","rule"):
                    expanded = [comp]
                else:
                    # unknown
                    eprint_error(f"Unknown style '{comp}'")
                    sys.exit(1)
                if sign=="+":
                    for e in expanded:
                        cur_set.add(e)
                else:
                    for e in expanded:
                        cur_set.discard(e)
            current = list(cur_set)
        else:
            # replace
            new_set = set()
            for p in parts:
                # p may have +/- but if not all_mod, we treat as replace starting empty, but +/- still affects empty?
                # For simplicity, handle +/- even in replace: + adds, - removes (from empty, removing does nothing)
                if p.startswith("+") or p.startswith("-"):
                    sign = p[0]
                    comp = p[1:]
                    if comp in ("header","default","full","auto","plain"):
                        if comp=="plain":
                            if sign=="+":
                                new_set.clear()
                            continue
                        elif comp=="default":
                            expanded = DEFAULT_STYLE
                        elif comp=="full":
                            expanded = FULL_STYLE
                        elif comp=="auto":
                            expanded = DEFAULT_STYLE
                        elif comp=="header":
                            expanded = ["header-filename"]
                        else:
                            expanded=[]
                    else:
                        if comp in ("changes","grid","header-filename","header-filesize","numbers","snip","rule"):
                            expanded=[comp]
                        else:
                            eprint_error(f"Unknown style '{comp}'")
                            sys.exit(1)
                    if sign=="+":
                        for e in expanded:
                            new_set.add(e)
                    else:
                        for e in expanded:
                            new_set.discard(e)
                else:
                    # no sign
                    if p in ("header","default","full","auto","plain"):
                        if p=="plain":
                            new_set.clear()
                        elif p=="default":
                            new_set.update(DEFAULT_STYLE)
                        elif p=="full":
                            new_set.update(FULL_STYLE)
                        elif p=="auto":
                            new_set.update(DEFAULT_STYLE)
                        elif p=="header":
                            new_set.add("header-filename")
                    else:
                        if p not in ("changes","grid","header-filename","header-filesize","numbers","snip","rule"):
                            eprint_error(f"Unknown style '{p}'")
                            sys.exit(1)
                        new_set.add(p)
            current = list(new_set)
    if current is None:
        # default
        current = DEFAULT_STYLE[:]
    return current

def format_file_size(size):
    if size < 1024:
        return f"{size} B"
    elif size < 1024*1024:
        return f"{size/1024:.1f} KiB"
    else:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024):.1f} MiB"

def tab_placeholder(width):
    if width==0: width=4
    if width==1: return "↹"
    if width==2: return "├┤"
    if width>=3: return "├"+"─"*(width-2)+"┤"
    return "↹"

def expand_tabs_simple(line, tab_width):
    if tab_width==0: return line
    res=[]; col=0
    for ch in line:
        if ch=='\t':
            spaces=tab_width-(col%tab_width)
            res.append(' '*spaces); col+=spaces
        else:
            res.append(ch); col+=1
    return "".join(res)

def strip_ansi(s):
    ansi=re.compile(r'\x1B(?:[@-Z\\-_]|\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~])')
    return ansi.sub('', s)

def show_all_line(line_str, notation, tab_width):
    res=[]
    col=0
    for ch in line_str:
        if ch==' ':
            res.append('·')
            col+=1
        elif ch==chr(9):
            tw = tab_width if tab_width!=0 else 4
            if tw==0:
                tw=4
            needed = tw - (col % tw)
            if needed==1:
                res.append('↹')
            else:
                res.append('├' + '─'*(needed-2) + '┤' if needed>=2 else '↹')
            col+=needed
        else:
            o=ord(ch)
            if o==0:
                res.append('␀' if notation=='unicode' else '^@')
                col+=1
            elif 1<=o<=31:
                if o==10:
                    res.append('␊' if notation=='unicode' else '^J')
                    col+=1
                elif o==13:
                    res.append('␍' if notation=='unicode' else '^M')
                    col+=1
                else:
                    if notation=='unicode':
                        res.append(chr(0x2400+o))
                    else:
                        if o<=26:
                            res.append('^'+chr(64+o))
                        elif o==27:
                            res.append('^[')
                        elif o==28:
                            res.append('^\\')
                        elif o==29:
                            res.append('^]')
                        elif o==30:
                            res.append('^^')
                        elif o==31:
                            res.append('^_')
                        else:
                            res.append(chr(0x2400+o))
                    col+=1
            elif o==127:
                res.append('␡' if notation=='unicode' else '^?')
                col+=1
            elif o>=128:
                if ch.isprintable():
                    res.append(ch)
                    col+=1
                else:
                    esc="\\x%02X" % o
                    res.append(esc)
                    col+=len(esc)
            else:
                res.append(ch)
                col+=1
    return "".join(res)

def parse_line_range_for_file(ranges, total):
    parsed=[]
    for spec in ranges:
        spec=spec.strip()
        if not spec: continue
        parts=spec.split(":")
        if len(parts)==1:
            try: n=int(parts[0]); parsed.append((n,n,0))
            except: eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}"); sys.exit(1)
        elif len(parts)==2:
            start_s,end_s=parts
            start=None; end=None
            if start_s!="":
                try: start=int(start_s)
                except: eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}"); sys.exit(1)
            if end_s!="":
                if end_s.startswith("+"):
                    if start is None: eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}"); sys.exit(1)
                    try: offset=int(end_s[1:]); end=start+offset
                    except: eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}"); sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    try: end=int(end_s)
                    except: eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}"); sys.exit(1)
            parsed.append((start,end,0))
        elif len(parts)==3:
            start_s,end_s,ctx_s=parts
            start=None; end=None; ctx=0
            if start_s!="":
                try: start=int(start_s)
                except: eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}"); sys.exit(1)
            if end_s!="":
                if end_s.startswith("+"):
                    if start is None: eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}"); sys.exit(1)
                    try: offset=int(end_s[1:]); end=start+offset
                    except: eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}"); sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    try: end=int(end_s)
                    except: eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}"); sys.exit(1)
            if ctx_s!="":
                try: ctx=int(ctx_s)
                except: eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}"); sys.exit(1)
            parsed.append((start,end,ctx))
        else:
            eprint_error(f"Invalid line range: {spec}"); sys.exit(1)
    expanded=[]
    for start,end,ctx in parsed:
        s=start; e=end
        if s is not None and s<0: s=total+s+1
        if e is not None and e<0: e=total+e+1
        if s is None: s=1
        if e is None: e=total
        if s<1: s=1
        if e<1: e=1
        if s>total: continue
        if e>total: e=total
        s=max(1,s-ctx)
        e=min(total,e+ctx)
        if s<=e: expanded.append((s,e))
    if not expanded: return [], []
    expanded_sorted=sorted(expanded)
    merged=[expanded_sorted[0]]
    for cur in expanded_sorted[1:]:
        prev=merged[-1]
        if cur[0]<=prev[1]+1: merged[-1]=(prev[0],max(prev[1],cur[1]))
        else: merged.append(cur)
    return merged, expanded_sorted

def parse_highlight_ranges(specs):
    res=[]
    for spec in specs:
        spec=spec.strip()
        if not spec: continue
        parts=spec.split(":")
        if len(parts)==1:
            try: n=int(parts[0]); res.append((n,n))
            except: eprint_error(f"Invalid highlight line: {spec}"); sys.exit(1)
        elif len(parts)==2:
            start_s,end_s=parts
            if start_s=="": start=1
            else:
                try: start=int(start_s)
                except: eprint_error(f"Invalid highlight line: {spec}"); sys.exit(1)
            if end_s=="": end=float('inf')
            else:
                if end_s.startswith("+"):
                    try: offset=int(end_s[1:]); end=start+offset
                    except: eprint_error(f"Invalid highlight line: {spec}"); sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    try: end=int(end_s)
                    except: eprint_error(f"Invalid highlight line: {spec}"); sys.exit(1)
            if not isinstance(end,float) and start>end: start,end=end,start
            res.append((start,end))
        else:
            eprint_error(f"Invalid highlight line: {spec}"); sys.exit(1)
    return res

def is_highlighted(ln, hl_ranges):
    for s,e in hl_ranges:
        if e==float('inf'):
            if ln>=s: return True
        else:
            if s<=ln<=e: return True
    return False

def read_config_file(path):
    opts=[]
    try:
        with open(path,'r',encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore') as f:
            for line in f:
                stripped=line.strip()
                if not stripped or stripped.startswith('#'): continue
                try:
                    parts=shlex.split(stripped, comments=False)
                    opts.extend(parts)
                except:
                    opts.extend(stripped.split())
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass
    return opts

def get_bat_opts():
    v=os.environ.get("BAT_OPTS")
    if not v: return []
    try: return shlex.split(v)
    except: return v.split()

DEFAULT_STYLE=["changes","grid","header-filename","numbers","snip"]
FULL_STYLE=["changes","grid","header-filename","header-filesize","numbers","snip","rule"]

def parse_style_list(raw_values):
    current=None
    for raw in raw_values:
        raw=raw.strip()
        if not raw:
            current=[]
            continue
        parts=[p.strip() for p in raw.split(",") if p.strip()!=""]
        if not parts:
            current=[]
            continue
        all_mod=all(p.startswith("+") or p.startswith("-") for p in parts)
        if all_mod and current is not None:
            cur_set=set(current)
            for p in parts:
                sign=p[0]; comp=p[1:]
                if comp=="plain":
                    if sign=="+": cur_set.clear()
                    continue
                if comp=="default": expanded=DEFAULT_STYLE
                elif comp=="full": expanded=FULL_STYLE
                elif comp=="auto": expanded=DEFAULT_STYLE
                elif comp=="header": expanded=["header-filename"]
                elif comp in ("changes","grid","header-filename","header-filesize","numbers","snip","rule"): expanded=[comp]
                else: eprint_error(f"Unknown style '{comp}'"); sys.exit(1)
                if sign=="+":
                    for e in expanded: cur_set.add(e)
                else:
                    for e in expanded: cur_set.discard(e)
            current=list(cur_set)
        else:
            new_set=set()
            for p in parts:
                if p.startswith("+") or p.startswith("-"):
                    sign=p[0]; comp=p[1:]
                    if comp=="plain":
                        if sign=="+": new_set.clear()
                        continue
                    elif comp=="default": expanded=DEFAULT_STYLE
                    elif comp=="full": expanded=FULL_STYLE
                    elif comp=="auto": expanded=DEFAULT_STYLE
                    elif comp=="header": expanded=["header-filename"]
                    elif comp in ("changes","grid","header-filename","header-filesize","numbers","snip","rule"): expanded=[comp]
                    else: eprint_error(f"Unknown style '{comp}'"); sys.exit(1)
                    if sign=="+":
                        for e in expanded: new_set.add(e)
                    else:
                        for e in expanded: new_set.discard(e)
                else:
                    if p=="plain": new_set.clear()
                    elif p=="default": new_set.update(DEFAULT_STYLE)
                    elif p=="full": new_set.update(FULL_STYLE)
                    elif p=="auto": new_set.update(DEFAULT_STYLE)
                    elif p=="header": new_set.add("header-filename")
                    else:
                        if p not in ("changes","grid","header-filename","header-filesize","numbers","snip","rule"): eprint_error(f"Unknown style '{p}'"); sys.exit(1)
                        new_set.add(p)
            current=list(new_set)
    if current is None:
        current=DEFAULT_STYLE[:]
    return current

def format_file_size(size):
    if size<1024: return f"{size} B"
    elif size<1024*1024: return f"{size/1024:.1f} KiB"
    else: return f"{size/(1024*1024):.1f} MiB"
